steps: Plan the design option

Choose standard, vented cavity or Komfort Zone Kit (KZK) before framing; the chamber and ceiling must be at least 88" for every option. Do any propane or Kozy Power Vent (KPV) conversion before framing — afterwards the control board has to come out.

Read the documentation for your design option before installing.

  • Standard installation: follow the sections marked "standard installation." Up to (2) heat transfer kits (HTK-EXT / HTK-INT, same or mixed) keep the standard framing; remove one rear square cover plate per kit.
  • Vented cavity: a minimum opening in the fireplace cavity reduces heat above the fireplace — allows combustible facing above, lower mantel clearances and less heat at a TV.
  • Komfort Zone Kit (#KZK-045 or #KZK-1510A): redistributes radiant heat through plenum(s); framing may differ — follow the kit manual.
  • Kozy Power Vent (#KPV): fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only; see its own manual.

Set it on a level surface that supports the fireplace and venting, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Bedroom installs are allowed. It is heavy: team lift, using the side lift handles (a 2" x 4" fits through them).

Outdoor covered installs: operation approved from 40°F to 110°F; the overhang in front and to each side must be at least 1/2 of the roofline height above the fireplace base; black painted safety barriers are recommended outdoors.

Manufactured (USA only) or mobile homes: allowed when aftermarket and permanently located, where local codes don't prohibit it.
Nailing flanges & stand-offs

Fit both nailing flanges (required for every installation, never removed) — their stand-offs give 3½" from the fireplace sides to framing. Install the stand-off assembly and header heat shield for standard and vented cavity installs.

1. Remove the (2) nailing flanges from the sides, align them with the holes on the outside corners (stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace) and screw them on through the slots.
  2. Bend the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face — never toward it.
  3. Position framing studs against the small stand-off on the back of each flange.
  4. Form the header heat shield and attach it to the stand-off assembly with (4) screws; fasten the stand-off assembly to the top of the fireplace with (4) screws.
  5. Form the back stand-off heat shields and re-secure them with the screws removed.
KZK installs: the header heat shield may be removed and discarded, but the top stand-off assembly and the back stand-offs must stay installed.
Rough framing

Minimum rough opening 46-1/4" H × 57-5/8" W × 22" D; enclosure height and base-to-ceiling 88". Set the fireplace on wood or a non-combustible surface (not linoleum or carpet); insulate outside walls against cold air.

Rough opening H × W × D46-1/4" × 57-5/8" × 22"
Enclosure height / base to ceiling88" / 88"
Finishing edge to ceiling60-1/2"
  • Same for all design options; allow for wall covering and facing thickness.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required; a hearth may be flush with the bottom finishing edge.
  • On carpet, tile or other combustibles (other than wood flooring), set it on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth of the appliance.
  • Raised installs need a solid, continuous platform; prepare the foundation for any masonry load.
  • TV recess: in tests, TV surface temperatures did not exceed 150°F with a 4¼" deep recess above the fireplace.

Vented cavity

  • Remove the (2) top cover plates and the convection baffle ((4) screws behind the upper edge of the opening).
  • Front option: a single 3" x 44" minimum air discharge opening. Top option: 1½" from the enclosure top to the ceiling on all three sides.
  • Only optional 1/2" x 1/2" hardware mesh (19 gauge or less) in the opening — no grilles or louvers, nothing covering it.
  • Sprinkler heads: at least 60" from the discharge opening at every point.
Note: the manual's text on p. 24 says the single 3" x 44" minimum air discharge opening can be at the front or at the rear, into an adjacent room; the caption for the rear option (Figure 3.17) on the same page gives a 3" x 52" minimum opening.
Vent framing & clearances

Keep 1" to combustibles on all sides of vertical pipe and on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe, and 16-1/4" from any venting to the enclosure top on horizontal terminations. Use listed wall thimbles; never recess the vent cap.

• Horizontal sections need 1/4" rise for every 12" of travel.
  • Wall pass-through: measure from the fireplace floor level to the vent center, then cut and frame so the pipe runs level through the wall. The minimum framing height is drawn in Figure 3.7 (p. 17), based on a Simpson DuraVent elbow; other elbows vary.
  • Metal Fab pipe needs adapter 5DDA, which raises the minimum vent-center height by 3-1/4" for horizontal pass-throughs.
  • Attic insulation shields and wall thimbles may be insulated with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136.
  • Exterior termination must meet the clearances in Section 6.2 (p. 42).
Massachusetts: sidewall-vented installs with the termination less than 7 feet above grade need carbon monoxide detectors and vent signage (Section 1.3, p. 7).
Facing & finishing

Non-combustible facing (up to 1/2" thick) is required at the top and sides, installed only up to the finishing edge so the glass frame stays removable. Screws may enter the outer shell up to 1/2" in the allowed areas.

Standard installation

  • Combustible mantel: 3/4" trim from 16" above the top finishing edge; 6" deep mantel from 19-1/2"; +1" of depth for every 1" of height above that.
  • Non-combustible mantel: minimum 6" above the top finishing edge at up to 6" deep, then 1" up for every 1" deeper.
  • Hearth: the bottom finishing edge can be flush with the top of a combustible hearth.
  • Side trim: 1" combustible trim from 3" off the side finishing edge; beyond 6", unlimited. Adjacent sidewall 6" minimum.

Vented cavity and KZK (baffle and cover plates removed)

  • 1" side trim may be flush with the side finishing edge; beyond 6", unlimited.
  • Combustible wall finish up to 1" thick over the required non-combustible material, down to the finishing edge and up to the discharge opening — never blocking it.
  • Mantel and hearth clearances are drawn in Figure 4.7 (p. 37).

To limit drywall cracking: dry, dust-free materials; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), fully cured; a high quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat; avoid flat or light-colored paints.
Gas line + leak test

Run the line through the gas access hole to a listed 1/2" tee-handle shut-off and flex connector on the 1/2" valve inlet (the fireplace comes with a 3/8" × 36" flex connector and shut-off); don't obstruct the fan. Check every joint with soapy water.

• Qualified installer, to local code or ANSI Z223.1; Massachusetts requires a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off from the piping. At ½ psi or less: close the appliance's manual shut-off to isolate it.
  • Manufactured for natural gas. For propane use the conversion kit (sold separately, LCK-BH44-SPB) and its instructions — before the panels, logs or light-kit parts go in.
  • High altitude: ask the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
Vent system & restrictor

Install a listed 5" × 8" co-axial system (or reduce to 4" × 6-5/8") within the vertical and horizontal limits and the termination clearances. If restriction is wanted, slide the restrictor plate into the 5" exhaust before attaching the vent (or later, through the baffle).

Approved: American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab (adapter 5DDA), Olympia Chimney Supply, Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent, rigid or flexible pipe; Kozy Power Vent #KPV (sold separately).

Vertical3' min / 50' max + cap
Vertical, 45° elbows with reducer10' min run · up to (4) 45° · no 90°
24" up + 90°6" – 24" horizontal
36" up + 90°6" – 8' horizontal
48" up + 90°6" – 12' horizontal
25' up + 90°6" – 25' horizontal
  • Must not share or connect to a chimney flue serving a solid-fuel appliance.
  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
  • Restrictor plate (components packet): shipped with all inner rings in, for the most restriction. Knock out the innermost ring for less, or all inner rings for the least. Bend the tabs to about 80° and insert it into the 5" exhaust in the firebox ceiling, tabs toward you.
  • Vertical cap height above the roof depends on pitch: 1.0 ft for flat to 6/12, up to 8.0 ft for over 20/12 to 21/12 (table on p. 41).
  • Termination clearances are in Section 6.2 (p. 42) — for example 12" above grade, and 12" (Canada) / 9" (US) to a window or door that opens.
Panels, logs & safety barrier

Install the refractory or black glass panels (required to operate), then the BH44-500 log set by the number on each log, keeping logs off the burner ports; add crushed glass, the (4) charred pieces, lava rock and rock wool embers. Hang the BH44-ES barrier, flush or recessed.

• Convert to propane first, if converting.
  • Panel clips ship flat: separate them at the perforations and bend the finger to 90°. Back panel first, then the sides (tilt the back in, pivot up; (2) clips per side).
  • Black glass: smooth side forward, textured side to the firebox; clean gloves, both hands; slide the sides along the main log support and check each sits flat.
  • Logs: BH44-1 at the rear against the log stop bracket flanges; BH44-2, -3 and -4 onto the burner studs; then BH44-5 to BH44-10 by their pins and notches (Figures 8.8–8.9, p. 52).
  • Rock wool embers go on with a steel or stiff-bristle nylon brush. Poor log placement affects the flame and causes excessive soot on the logs and glass.
  • Barrier: align the notched tabs with the (4) slots on the glass valance for a flush or recessed mount, raise the front slightly and let the tabs drop in.

Never run the fireplace without the panel kit, or with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
Power & control setup

Supply 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps to the junction box — always hot, no switch, properly grounded. Rocker switch OFF, (4) AA in the backup holder, (3) AAA in the remote, connect AC power; clear packaging from the firebox, then sync the remote and set the switch to ON.

1. Lift off the safety screen to reach the ON/OFF toggle switch and remote learn (sync) button on the left side.
  2. Press the sync button: the module beeps (3) times and an amber LED lights.
  3. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps confirm the code and the pilot lights.
  4. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command. The system is initialized.
  5. Set the toggle switch to ON for remote operation and reinstall the safety screen.
  • On battery backup only the burner runs; the fan, top light and ember bed light need 120V.
  • The (4)-outlet junction box on the left side (KPV, ember bed light kit, control module) is behind a (4)-screw access cover.
  • Ember bed light: remove the media tray and fit the (6) halogen bulbs into the lamp bases; top light: (2) halogen bulbs. Never touch bulbs bare-handed.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet pressure at tap IN (A) with all other gas appliances on, and manifold pressure at tap OUT (B), using a ¼" I.D. hose. Then re-seal each tap: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten), then relight and confirm with the manometer that the tap is sealed (it should read no pressure). Burn 15 minutes, then set the venturis or restrictor for lazy, yellow flames.

Inlet NG / LP5" – 10.5" / 12" – 13" WC
Manifold NG low – high1.1" – 3.8" WC
Manifold LP low – high2.9" – 11" WC

Factory venturi openings

NG center / side3/16" / 3/16"
LP center / side1/2" / 5/8"
  • Dark orange flames with black tips: venturi closed too far — open slightly.
  • Short, blue flames: venturi open too far — close slightly.
  • Lifting (ghosting) flames: gas pressure too high (check the manometer) or venturi closed too far.
  • Short, flickering flames: excessive draft — add the restrictor plate. Lifting from insufficient draft: remove inner ring(s) or the plate.
  • Soot on the logs: check log placement before touching the venturi.
Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician only. Let the fireplace cool before each adjustment — slight changes give dramatic results. If flames still lift after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent, shut off the gas and call a qualified technician.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or use battery backup with fully charged batteries
Wiring disconnection → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check the shut-off valves; there may be more than one between appliance and main line
No propane or low gas pressure (bent line, undersized pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot not reaching the flame sensor → pilot screw on the valve: clockwise smaller, counterclockwise larger; seal it without over-tightening

panels.title: Burner won't light / no response
items: ON/OFF rocker switch off → set it to ON
Gas off or low, or propane tank empty → check for multiple shut-offs; refill
Faulty wiring or plugged main burner orifice → correct the wiring; remove the blockage
Remote not working or no call for heat → new batteries; remote on, thermostat operation off
No reaction to commands → low batteries, lost remote link (re-sync) or too many failed ignitions (reset the IFC)

panels.title: Goes out while running
items: No propane in tank
Glass assembly installed incorrectly
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked
Horizontal vent without ¼" rise per foot
Exhaust leaking back into the firebox → find and repair
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor

panels.title: Soot or blue, lifting flames
items: Soot on glass from log placement → re-set the logs
Venturi air shutter → open slightly for more air in the mix
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked
Vent pipes leaking or cap full of debris → repair or clear

codes: Backup pack below 4V; a low double-beep sounds on ON/OFF commands — replace the batteries
No ignition after two attempts — verify the gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted, then reset or re-initialize the control

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an ignition device sparks the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday use

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote. A single beep confirms the command.
  2. About 4 seconds later the control starts sparking at the pilot, and the fireplace lights.
  3. Press ON/OFF again to turn it off. The screen goes back to showing just the room temperature.
If the remote won't light the burner, check that the ON/OFF switch (left side, behind the safety screen) is set to ON.

First start, or after the gas was turned off

  1. Turn the fireplace off with the remote's ON/OFF key, then turn off all electric power to it.
  2. Turn the manual gas valve your technician installed clockwise to OFF.
  3. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  4. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on and press ON/OFF on the remote.

If it won't light

The control makes two tries of about 60 seconds each, then locks out. To reset, press ON/OFF to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds and press it again. If it still won't work, turn the fireplace off at the remote, turn the gas valve clockwise to OFF and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs the fireplace. Press the mode key to step through the features and use the arrow keys to change them. A single beep confirms most commands.

  • Flame height: there are 6 flame levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one level, down to off; the up arrow raises it one step. If the flame is off while the system is on, the up arrow relights it on high (HI).
  • Thermostat: press the thermostat key. The screen shows the room and set temperatures; use the arrows to change the set temperature.
  • Smart thermostat: press the thermostat key until SMART appears. It adjusts the flame height and turns the flame down as the room reaches your setting. You can't adjust the flame by hand while it's on.
  • Split flow: mode key to the split flow icon; the up arrow turns the secondary burner on, the down arrow turns it off.
  • Key lock: press mode and the up arrow together to lock or unlock the keys. A lock icon shows while it's on.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press the thermostat and mode keys together.
Batteries: the remote takes 3 AAA batteries. A battery icon appears on the screen before they run out.

firstfire.title: First fires: what's normal
firstfire.html:
Fog on the glass

When the fireplace is first lit, condensation appears on the glass. This happens with all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time to help the paint cure faster.

Ticks and pings

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you may hear noises. That's normal and doesn't affect how well the fireplace works or how long it lasts.

Flame color

On first lighting the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. Lazy, yellow flames are what you want.

Call a qualified service technician if the flames stay blue, lift off the burner, or turn dark orange with black, sooty tips. Adjusting the burner's air setting is a technician-only job.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The manual lists glass cleaning as a once-a-year job you can do yourself. Start only when the fireplace is completely cool: never remove or clean the glass while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Use the provided latch tool to release the two spring-loaded latches, tilt the top of the glass frame forward and lift it off the bottom rail.
  4. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Set the frame back on the bottom rail, tilt it in, and pull both latches closed with the tool. Put the safety screen back.
Never run the fireplace without the safety screen, or with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Don't strike or slam the glass. A damaged glass assembly is replaced as a complete unit by a qualified service person.
Note: p. 49 says the two spring-loaded latches that hold the glass are at the top of the firebox; the yearly firebox check on p. 70 says to inspect and operate the bottom latch assembly.

pilot.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
pilot.html:
The remote lets you choose how the pilot behaves:

IPIa spark lights the pilot each time the fireplace turns on
CPI (continuous pilot)the pilot stays lit even when the burner is off

CPI keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less air-flow disruption. If the pilot won't go out and you don't want it on, switch to IPI.

Check or change the mode

  • With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote's screen means CPI. No snowflake means IPI.
  • To change it, turn the system off, press the mode key until the CPI icon shows, then press the up arrow for CPI or the down arrow for IPI. A single beep confirms.

Normal pilot behavior

  • In CPI, if the burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns itself off as a safety feature. Every time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.
  • Within 24 hours of continuous pilot operation, the system turns off for about 5 seconds to run a safety check, then carries out your last command again.

fan.title: Fan and accent lights
fan.html:
Set these from the remote: press the mode key to reach the icon, then use the arrow keys.

Fan

  • The fan has 6 speeds. The arrows turn it on, off, or change the speed.
  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the fireplace lights so heat can build up, and keeps running about 12 minutes after the fireplace turns off.
  • Manual mode: the fan runs at its last setting, with no delay starting or stopping.
  • Leave the fan off during the first few hours of burning so the paint can cure.

Lights

  • Top accent light: the light icon; 6 brightness levels.
  • Ember-bed light: the AUX icon; the up arrow turns it on, the down arrow turns it off. To change its brightness, lift off the safety screen and turn the knob on the left side of the firebox: counterclockwise for dimmer, clockwise for brighter. Put the screen back afterwards.
The fan and lights don't work on battery backup during a power outage. The bulbs are halogen: never touch them with bare hands.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power, with a backup battery pack so the burner still works when the power goes out.

Backup pack (on the control module)4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

During an outage

Only the burner runs on the backup batteries. The fan, top light and ember-bed light won't work until the power comes back.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: the fireplace gives a low double beep when you press ON/OFF, and won't accept any commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when the new batteries are in.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the batteries run out. It disappears when you replace them.

How long batteries last depends on their quality and how many times the fireplace lights.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell around the fireplace, including next to the floor: some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass causes burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety barrier screen on. If it's damaged, replace it with the Hussong barrier made for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely. If someone at risk lives with you, a safety gate can keep them away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable away, and never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • Turn the gas valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean more frequent cleaning.

What the technician checks every year

  • The firebox, vacuumed and cleaned of debris
  • The vent system, with nothing blocking combustion or ventilation air
  • Burner and pilot, vacuumed, with gas connections checked for leaks
  • The main burner lighting within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, with steady flames that don't lift or float
  • The flame safety system shutting off within 30 seconds
  • The glass, for cracks, scratches and nicks

Every 6 months

A qualified service person disconnects and vacuums the fan. Its bearings are sealed and never need oil.

Your part: clean the glass once a year, and keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, including gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. (Kozy Heat) gives the original purchaser a limited lifetime warranty, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship.

30 days · parts and laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborall other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is paid only to an authorized dealer. Keep your proof of purchase showing the date, with the fireplace's serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Installation not done by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not following the manual
  • A removed serial number or testing label, or any alteration
  • Water damage, submersion or long periods of dampness
  • Installation and site problems such as inadequate venting, excessive offsets or negative air pressure
  • A change of owner: the warranty can't be transferred
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are on the warranty page of the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min / max5" / 10.5" WC
Natural gas recommended7" WC
Propane min / max12" / 13" WC
Propane recommended12" WC (Table 5.1)

Read at the valve tap marked IN (A) with a ¼" I.D. hose, pilot and burner lit, and all other gas appliances in the house on or at full capacity. Then turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose and tighten the tap screw clockwise: snug, don't over-tighten. Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to the tap (A) to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.

Too high or too low: contact the gas company — only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure. Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off for piping tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC
Propane low / high2.9" / 11" WC

Read at the valve tap marked OUT (B): light the pilot, open the tap, attach the manometer with a ¼" I.D. hose and light the burner. Afterwards turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the tap screw clockwise: snug, don't over-tighten. Relight pilot and burner and attach the manometer to the tap (B) to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Lifting (ghosting) flames can mean the gas pressure is too high — check the manometer settings.

  • Horizontal runs: ¼" rise per 12".
  • Class A (min 7" ID) or masonry chimney conversion: 4" aluminum flex, 10' min / 50' max, 0" – 24" horizontal (p. 48).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Top, side and back stand-off brackets0"

Floor protection in front of the fireplace isn't required. Corner installations are drawn in Figure 3.4 (p. 14). Keep sprinkler heads at least 60" from a vented cavity discharge opening.

specMantel.title: Mantel and trim (standard installation)
specMantel.html:
¾" combustible mantel trim16" above top finishing edge
6" deep combustible mantel19-1/2" above top finishing edge
Deeper mantels+1" depth per 1" of height
Non-combustible mantel6" above, up to 6" deep; then 1" up per 1" deeper
1" combustible side trimfrom 3" off the side finishing edge; unlimited beyond 6"
Finishing edge to ceiling60-1/2"

A combustible hearth may be flush with the bottom finishing edge. Vented cavity and KZK installs use their own chart (Figure 4.7, p. 37) and allow 1" side trim flush with the side finishing edge.

specFraming.title: Rough opening and enclosure
specFraming.html:
Min rough opening height46-1/4"

The same for every design option; size the opening to allow for wall covering and facing thickness. Set on wood or a non-combustible surface (not linoleum or carpet). The appliance dimensions, including the gas line and electrical access holes, are given as a drawing (Figure 2.1, p. 9).

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Backup battery pack4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

The supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it. Ground to local code, or the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1; the three-prong plug goes into a properly grounded receptacle. The (4)-outlet junction box on the left side feeds the Kozy Power Vent, ember bed light kit and control module. On battery backup only the burner works.

review.notes: Manual pages 2, 4, 6 and 75 are blank. Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: efficiency (63.87% NG / 64.43% LP AFUE), weight (330 lb), heating area. Figure 2.1 (p. 9) gives the appliance dimensions only as drawing labels (20", 22", 35¼", 46¼", 50⅝", 57⅝", 44 7/16", 24 7/8"…); the text doesn't say which is height, width or depth, so the guide points to the drawing instead of labelling them. The catalog H/W/D (35.25 / 50.625 / 20) and view area (44-7/16" x 24 7/8") numbers all appear on that drawing but couldn't be confirmed; the only glass size in the text is the 23.75" x 41.75" glass part (p. 72). Drawing-only content not transcribed: Figure 3.7 wall pass-through height (p. 17), Figure 3.4 corner installation (p. 14), Figures 4.1 / 4.5 finishing dimensions (pp. 30, 34), Figure 4.7 vented cavity / KZK mantel chart (p. 37), Figures 3.20 / 3.23 overhang alternatives (pp. 26, 28), the Figure 7.2 combination-venting shaded area (p. 47) and the flame-appearance photos (pp. 66, 71). Table 5.1 (p. 40) prints "recommended" under the propane 12" WC minimum with no separate value, while Table 11.1 (p. 65) lists propane 12"–13" WC min–max; the guide shows 12" – 13" and only the natural gas 7" WC recommendation. Metric labels differ for the same inch values (57-5/8" printed as 1463, 1464 and 1468mm; 46-1/4" as 1174 and 1175mm; pp. 9, 14, 15, 33); the guide uses inches only. Manual errors left out of the guide: the table of contents lists an 8.3 "Safety Barrier Installation" section that isn't in the body, so its 8.x numbering differs, and its page numbers run one page high from there on; p. 29 points to "Section 4.10 … page 44" (it is 4.3, p. 36); p. 43 points to Section 3.6 "on page 41" (p. 16); p. 68 points to Section 9.0 "on page 67" (p. 55); p. 69 calls the log-set section 8.5 (body 8.4, p. 51); 10.9.5 "Turn OFF the appliance" (p. 62) repeats the turn-on wording ("with the system in the OFF position … to turn ON"), so the guide says press ON/OFF to turn it off, per that section's described result; the 10.9.8 split-flow steps are numbered 4–6 (p. 63). The manual calls the standard (non-power-vent) direct-vent setup "natural draft"; Kozy Power Vent #KPV, the KZK kits, the HTK kits and the LCK-BH44-SPB conversion have their own manuals, not included. The manual doesn't say which pilot mode (IPI or CPI) is the factory setting, or whether the fan, top light and ember-bed light are standard (the catalog says standard; the ember-bed bulbs are "included in component packet", the top-light bulbs "included with this kit"). Only the BH44-500 log set is covered (the catalog also mentions a birch set). Massachusetts requirements (p. 7) are summarized only in the vent-framing step. Remote flame-modulation, light-modulation and thermostat deactivation procedures (pp. 62–64) and the 10.3 manual-operation reset (p. 59) are left to the manual.
